key_insight: Coupling parametric finite elements with symplectic Runge–Kutta methods yields high-order curve evolution with provably exact enclosed-area conservation.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports accurate simulation of area-conserving interface relaxation driven by surface diffusion.
method: Discretize the classical BGN formulation using parametric finite elements.
Apply q-stage Gauss Runge–Kutta integration for temporal order 2q without added conservation constraints.
Solve the fully implicit nonlinear system using an equivalent formulation and monolithic damped Newton iteration.
evidence_signal: Tests on various evolving curves confirm exact area preservation, high-order temporal convergence, and favorable mesh quality, with Newton iteration counts rapidly falling below 8 per step.
watch_item: Each time step requires a strongly nonlinear implicit solve, and the abstract does not establish unconditional discrete perimeter decrease.
paper_title: High-Order Area-Preserving Runge--Kutta Methods for Surface Diffusion Flow of Curves
